summary: Jupiter is a native macOS SwiftUI app that scans the user's home directory for reclaimable disk space across ten categories (caches, logs, Xcode, package managers, Docker, snapshots, etc.) and moves selected items to Trash instead of deleting them permanently.
The UI is a custom shell (ShellView) with a sidebar and a detail pane; ScanViewModel owns scan/clean state and runs all heavy work off the main actor.
Scanner.scanAll runs all category scans concurrently and reconciles overlapping paths so the same bytes are never counted twice; PathIndex memoises measured sizes.
Cleaner moves items to Trash (or runs docker prune / tmutil for snapshots) from a detached task and returns per-item outcomes, which ScanViewModel applies on the main actor.
A separate Memory page observes vm_stat/swap and runs a polite purge ladder (/bin/sync then /usr/sbin/purge) without quitting apps.
A background Watchdog installs a launchd LaunchAgent that periodically runs Jupiter headless (--watchdog-run) to auto-clean Safe caches, with a lock file preventing overlap.
Privileged commands go through PrivilegedRunner, which tries sudo -n, then sudo -A with an askpass helper, then osascript, caching the sudo ticket while the app is open.
There are zero third-party dependencies; sizes are measured as st_blocks × 512 allocated bytes.

interview.pitch: Jupiter is a native macOS cleaner I built in SwiftUI with zero third-party dependencies. It scans ten categories concurrently, measures real allocated bytes using st_blocks times 512, and moves everything to Trash so nothing is permanently deleted. The UI never blocks because scanning and cleaning run off the main actor, and clean results are applied back on the main actor in one pass. There is also a Memory page that runs a polite purge ladder and a background Watchdog that uses launchd to auto-clean Safe caches even when the app is closed.
tradeoffs: Sizes are allocated bytes, not logical sizes, so numbers differ from Finder and may look larger.
Full Disk Access is detected by probing Mail/Messages directories, which is a heuristic rather than a permission API.
Snapshot sizes are reported as zero because tmutil does not report per-snapshot bytes; actual freed space is measured by disk delta.
The sudo ticket cache is only five minutes by default, so privileged purges may still prompt after inactivity.
Watchdog runs only Safe or optionally Okay items and never Risky, so large Risky categories are never auto-cleaned.

questions.q: How do you avoid double-counting overlapping paths?
questions.a: Scanner.reconcile runs after all categories finish; the first category to claim a path keeps its bytes and later rows are rebuilt with size zero and a detail saying already counted. PathIndex also memoises measured sizes.

questions.q: Why move to Trash instead of deleting?
questions.a: The README and Cleaner both use FileManager.trashItem so files stay recoverable; only files already in ~/.Trash are removed permanently.

questions.q: How does cleaning stay off the main thread?
questions.a: confirmClean wraps Cleaner.clean in Task.detached; the cleaner works on plain CleanTarget values and returns outcomes, and ScanViewModel.apply runs on the MainActor.

questions.q: How does the background watchdog work?
questions.a: JupiterApp.init checks for --watchdog-run and calls WatchdogRunner.runAndExit, which scans a fast subset of categories and cleans allowed safeties. LaunchAgentInstaller writes a plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents and bootstraps it with launchctl.

questions.q: How are privileged purges handled without prompting every time?
questions.a: PrivilegedRunner first tries sudo -n, then sudo -A with an askpass helper that shows the macOS password sheet, then osascript. After success it schedules a background ticket refresh every two minutes.

questions.q: What is the Memory page doing?
questions.a: MemoryLab.observe reads vm_stat and sysctl; runLadder runs /bin/sync, optionally /usr/sbin/purge via PrivilegedRunner, waits, then re-observes and reports the honest available-memory delta.

prompt:
# duggal1/jupiter

## Purpose

Jupiter is a native macOS SwiftUI storage cleaner that scans the user's home directory across ten reclaimable-space categories and moves selected items to Trash instead of permanently deleting them. Scanning and cleaning run off the main actor, with a Memory page for page-cache reclamation and a launchd-backed background Watchdog for scheduled Safe-cache cleaning. There are zero third-party dependencies.

## Module map

| Module | Path | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| App Entry Point | `Purge` | `@main` scene; `--watchdog-run` headless entry |
| SwiftUI Shell | `Purge/Views` | Sidebar/detail routing between Clean, Watchdog, Memory panes |
| Scan View Model | `Purge/ViewModels` | Main-actor scan/clean state, selection batches, progress streaming |
| Scanner Engine | `Purge/Scanner` | Concurrent per-category scanning, allocated-size measurement, path reconciliation |
| Junk Model | `Purge/Models` | `ScannedItem`/`CleanTarget`, `JunkItem`/`JunkCategory`, `Safety`, `CleanAction` |
| Cleaner | `Purge/Scanner` | Trash moves, `tmutil` snapshot thinning, coalesced `docker prune`, per-item outcomes |
| Path Index | `Purge/Scanner` | Memoised path sizes and ownership tracking to avoid double-counting |
| Docker Scanner | `Purge/Scanner` | Docker build-cache and daemon rows; `docker prune` subcommands |
| Memory Lab | `Purge/Scanner` | `vm_stat`/swap reads; `/bin/sync` + `/usr/sbin/purge` ladder |
| Memory View Model | `Purge/ViewModels` | Observable Memory page state and freed-byte reporting |
| Watchdog Subsystem | `Purge/Scanner` | Headless scheduled cleaner, launchd agent, config, run logging |
| Privileged Runner | `Purge/Scanner` | `sudo` tiers and `osascript` fallback; sudo ticket cache |

## Request path

1. User triggers a scan from the Clean pane; `ScanViewModel` (main actor) starts it.
2. `Scanner.scanAll` resets `PathIndex`, runs all category scans concurrently, measures allocated bytes via `st_blocks × 512`.
3. After categories finish, `Scanner.reconcile` resolves overlapping paths so the first claimant keeps bytes and later rows become size zero.
4. Results stream into `ScanViewModel` state; UI renders categories and selectable items.
5. User confirms clean; `ScanViewModel.confirmClean` wraps `Cleaner.clean` in `Task.detached`.
6. `Cleaner` moves items to Trash, runs `docker prune`, or thins snapshots via `tmutil`, streaming progress.
7. `ScanViewModel.apply` runs on `MainActor`, applying per-item outcomes to UI state.

## Rules

- Heavy scan and clean work must run off the main actor; only state application (`ScanViewModel.apply`) happens on `MainActor`.
- `Scanner` owns size measurement and path reconciliation; `PathIndex` owns memoisation and ownership claims. New size logic belongs in `Purge/Scanner`.
- `Cleaner` is the only module that performs deletion/trash/prune; UI and view models must not call `FileManager.trashItem` or `tmutil` directly.
- Privileged commands must go through `PrivilegedRunner`; `MemoryLab` and snapshot thinning rely on it rather than shelling out themselves.
- Docker interaction is isolated in `DockerScanner`; `Scanner` and `Cleaner` delegate to it rather than invoking `docker` directly.
- Watchdog invokes `Scanner.scanWatchdog` and `Cleaner.clean` (see `WatchdogRunner`); it must not reimplement scanning or deletion.
- `PrivilegedRunner` must not be called from SwiftUI views directly; route through view models.

## External services

- Trash/filesystem via `FileManager.trashItem` — owned by `Cleaner`.
- `docker` CLI (build cache, images, containers, volumes, prune) — owned by `DockerScanner`.
- `tmutil` (snapshot thinning) — owned by `Cleaner`.
- `launchd` / `launchctl` (LaunchAgent install/bootstrap) — owned by `LaunchAgentInstaller` in Watchdog.
- `sudo` / `osascript` (privileged commands) — owned by `PrivilegedRunner`.
- `/bin/sync`, `/usr/sbin/purge` (memory ladder) — owned by `MemoryLab` via `PrivilegedRunner`.
- `vm_stat` / `sysctl` (memory observation) — owned by `MemoryLab`.

## Known weak spots

- Sizes are allocated bytes (`st_blocks × 512`), not logical sizes, so numbers differ from Finder and may appear larger.
- Full Disk Access detection probes Mail/Messages directories heuristically; not a permission API.
- Snapshot sizes report as zero because `tmutil` gives no per-snapshot bytes; freed space is inferred from disk delta.
- Sudo ticket cache defaults to five minutes, so privileged purges may prompt after inactivity.
- Watchdog cleans only Safe (optionally Okay) items and never Risky categories, so large Risky categories are never auto-cleaned.
- No idempotency is evident for trash operations; re-running a clean on already-trashed paths is not guarded.
- Snapshot size state can drift from actual disk usage since sizes are not measured directly.
- `PrivilegedRunner` caches the sudo ticket only while the app is open; background `--watchdog-run` invocations do not share it.
